title: Not knowing the tune: 'Breeze' at Preservation Hall
summary: Jim Robinson as melody carrier, and a night when the band struggled with a request.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You know somebody was telling me and I didn't get this directly from Jim you might want to check up on this Jim now is supposed to be complaining because he has to play the melody because nobody else does you know and he then just swings back to the melody to help everybody

out. Yeah I'm not trying to criticize Jim because Jim's my favorite trombonist I'm not trying to make them I don't like his style or anything but there are tunes that he doesn't know there was one tune funny over at Preservation Hall last night Breeze I guess somebody requested the 1920s tune Breeze let's see Winnie Manone made a record I can't remember any other records hardly

so the guys didn't know it and let me see who started out playing it Frog Joseph was there I think maybe he knew the melody maybe he played the chorus the first and then Sales tried to yell out the chords to them and Sales knew it halfway right I believe he sang a chorus but I didn't hear it I heard everybody laughing there the audience and all too Sales would be thumping out the chords like B flat A flat and all of a sudden he said like say maybe C oh sorry sorry excuse me sorry he yelled out to everybody

but then Emma went ahead and Emma played maybe Emma sang it I forgot who sang the chord it wasn't too bad as I say you know considering they didn't know the number that again is a characteristic of the New Orleans musicians they try to they know they're there to please the public
anything that they can if they halfway know it if the audience wants to hear it that's why they'll play stuff

tune over again, as I said, Bunk would do four or five times, maybe, or three or four times, quite often anyway, over and over again. If the audience and the dancers keep applauding a lot, they'd better hear it again.
